scenes.name: beat1_hook
scenes.text: Microsoft just went down worldwide again today! Over one hundred and thirty thousand enterprise users were kicked out of Teams, Outlook, and Copilot. But this time... it was not a cyberattack or CrowdStrike.

scenes.name: beat2_incident_mo
scenes.text: Microsoft tracked the chaos under incident M-O 1550821. It started when a backend cluster experienced sudden latency, causing automated health checks to fail.

scenes.name: beat3_cascading_crash
scenes.text: Instead of throttling traffic, the orchestrator automatically pulled those servers offline! That dumped one hundred percent of global traffic onto surviving nodes, creating an instant cascading collapse!

scenes.name: beat4_manual_reroute
scenes.text: The secure handshake proxies choked. Microsoft engineers had to manually bypass broken routing and force healthy capacity back into the cluster to halt the spiral.

scenes.name: beat5_engineering_lesson
scenes.card_sub: Never Let Health Checks Kill Clusters
scenes.text: The golden rule of distributed systems: Never let your health checks kill more than twenty percent of your fleet at once. Subscribe to TechStack AI for real engineering post-mortems!
